page: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a Gen7 storage-optimized instance powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8559C processor built on x86_64 architecture. Managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 2 physical cores driving 4 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading support. The server is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio. Local storage is provided by a bundled 937 GB NVMe SSD, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps. Advanced vector and matrix instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (tile and int8) are natively enabled alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration.

In single-threaded benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier responsiveness, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2299.0 and strong throughput in single-threaded gzip and bzip3 data compression tests. Multi-core performance is limited by its 2 physical core count, placing multi-threaded stress-ng execution and software compilation benchmarks in middle to lower tiers. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth measures at 33.73 GB/sec, while write bandwidth reaches 35.58 GB/sec. Application benchmarks demonstrate consistent mid-tier output, with Redis SET operations achieving 6.18 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 8.15 GB/sec.

By combining local NVMe SSD capacity with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory on a 4 vCPU configuration, the instance delivers high resource density for disk-bound and memory-sensitive services without requiring external block storage attachments. The core balance trades multi-threaded parallel throughput for single-threaded efficiency and high local I/O performance. The i7i.xlarge is well-suited for transactional databases, key-value caches like Redis, text processing systems, and local indexing workloads where storage latency and single-thread speed take priority.
